category_title: Middle school students with severe reading disabilities who disengage from traditional tasks
student_description: This 13-year-old student has severe reading disabilities that cause him to become passive, 'invisible,' and frustrated during traditional pen-to-paper tasks. He uniquely requires age-appropriate digital tools with multimodal options (images, audio, text prediction) to bypass writing barriers, alongside tight timelines and peer-sharing to motivate him.

criteria.rationale: To transition from needing a scribe to working autonomously, this student requires ongoing access to tools that reduce the cognitive load of spelling and typing.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan integrates assistive writing features, such as text prediction or autocorrect, to support the student's writing autonomy.

criteria.rationale: The student frequently loses physical work, which triggers frustration and withdrawal; a digital portfolio prevents this and supports multimedia inputs.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan establishes a centralized digital storage solution (e.g., a digital notebook) that supports multimedia (photos, voice memos) to organize work and prevent lost assignments.

criteria.rationale: Tight timelines create a sense of urgency that shifts the student's motivation and prevents passive disengagement.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan incorporates tight, structured timelines for task completion to maintain the student's momentum and motivation.

criteria.rationale: Knowing his work will be seen by peers provides a powerful motivational shift for this student, encouraging him to complete tasks.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan includes opportunities for the student's work to be shared publicly with peers (e.g., presented on a large screen) to increase accountability and motivation.
